subject.title: Orphaned lock files not cleared on gateway restart when PID matches current process

question: Should current-PID session locks that are not tracked in memory be reclaimed during gateway startup/recovery, and should this issue stay the focused tracker or move under the run-lifecycle reliability umbrella?
rationale: Source evidence confirms a partial cleanup, but reclaiming locks owned by the live gateway is a transcript data-integrity and recovery-policy choice that automation should not decide.

options.title: Keep Focused Tracker
options.body: Keep this issue open for same-PID restart/recovery lock semantics while maintainers decide the safe reclaim rule and repair or replace the linked PR.

options.title: Fold Into Lifecycle Umbrella
options.body: Move the remaining live-holder lock behavior to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/101863 only after preserving this issue's field evidence there.

options.title: Accept Boot Slice Only
options.body: Declare the matching-starttime startup cleanup sufficient and open a new, narrower issue for runtime/recovery live current-PID leaks.

recommendation.title: Keep Focused Tracker
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for same-PID restart/recovery lock semantics while maintainers decide the safe reclaim rule and repair or replace the linked PR.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the clearest recent commit-history connection to session-lock contention and cleanup in the central code paths.
